## Assessment of Personalizable Traits
::: callout-note
Selected Categories: Craving, Motivation, Emotion
:::

### Craving
- We could reword the Penn Alcohol Craving Scale, with timeline restricted to the last week (or even last two weeks).

- How often have you thought about drinking or about how good a drink would make you feel during this period?
- At its most severe point, how strong was your craving during this period?
- How much time have you spent thinking about drinking or about how good a drink would make you feel during this period?
- How difficult would it have been to resist taking a drinking during this period of time if you had known a bottle were in your house?
- Keeping in mind your responses to the previous questions, please rate your overall average alcohol craving for the stated period of time.

### Motivation
There is the 19 item [The Stages of Change Readiness and Treatment Eagerness Scale](https://www.drugsandalcohol.ie/26826/1/socratesv8.pdf) fount in SAMHSA Tip 35

They also have the readiness to change questionnaire which is shorter 12 items [link](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK571063/bin/A2_p160.pdf)


### Emotion
- DERS 16?

Based on last discussion, we're planning on selecting items from published scales to create our own overall measure.
:::

#### Acceptability of Intervention Measure (AIM)

#### Intervention Appropriateness Measure (IAM)

#### Feasibility of Intervention Measure (FIM)

[Measure Link](https://dissemination-implementation.org/assessment-instrument/acceptability-of-intervention-measure-aim)

CFA was assessed for each individual scale in study 2 of scale development, with lowest factor loading item dropped to trim the scale (to present 4 item scales). Cronbach's alpha for trimmed scales: acceptability = .85, appropriateness = .91, and feasibility = .89. \[Note: item wordings are very similar, so expected high alpha\].

Overall scale was fitted for a CFA, and a 3-factor model emerged as best fit compared with 1 and 2 factor models (acceptable fit, CFI = .96, RMSEA = .08, BIC = 8499.4). Several factors *are* highly correlated, with acceptabilty and appropriateness at .77 and appropriateness and feasibility at .

Study 3 reveals acceptable test-retest reliability: acceptability = .83, appropriateness = .87, and feasibility = .88. Median time between responses was 7 weeks.

##### Full Scale Items

AIM

- (INTERVENTION) meets my approval
- (INTERVENTION) is appealing to me.
- I like (INTERVENTION).
- I welcome (INTERVENTION).

IAM

- (INTERVENTION) seems fitting.
- (INTERVENTION) seems suitable.
- (INTERVENTION) seems applicable.
- (INTERVENTION) seems like a good match.

FIM

- (INTERVENTION) seems implementable.
- (INTERVENTION) seems possible.
- (INTERVENTION) seems doable.
- (INTERVENTION) seems easy to use.

##### Item Selection

- I approve of (INTERVENTION) #changed wording from original first AIM item
- (INTERVENTION) is appealing to me.
- (INTERVENTION) seems suitable.
- (INTERVENTION) seems applicable.
- (INTERVENTION) seems possible.
- (INTERVENTION) seems doable.

#### Credibility/Expectancy Questionnaire

2-factor model emerged from factor analysis - focused on the factor that I'm interested in pulling items out here. 3 items, loading range from .71 (How succesffully do you think this treatment will be in reducing your symptoms) to .88 (How confident would you be in recommending this treatment to a friend). .84 for the other item (how logical does the therapy offered to you seem). Factor was labelled credibility. Cronbach's alpha = .81 (total scale = .84). Acceptable test-retest: credibility r(67) = .75, p \< .001, but was assessed only 1 week apart.

##### Credibility Scale Items

- How logical does the therapy offered to you seem
- How successfully do you think this treatment will be in reducing your symptoms
- How confident would you be in recommending this treatment to a friend

##### Item Selection
- I think this intervention will successfully reduce my symptoms.
- I will recommend this treatment to a friend. 

## Other Assessments

#### General Artificial Intelligence Attitude (GAIA-15)

[Measure Link](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S2451958826001703?via%3Dihub#tbl3)

Moderate positive correlation with general AI use and specific AI use. Moderate marginal reliability, and unidimensional structure supported.

##### Full Scale Items

- I am impressed by what AI can do.
- I am interested in using AI in my daily life.
- AI is exciting.
- I shiver with discomfort with I think about the future uses of AI (R)
- When I think about AI, I have mostly positive feelings.
- I would invest my money in a bank that is exclusively managed by AI.
- I would buy an artwork painted by AI at an auction.
- To decide how to prioritize aid during humanitarian crises, I would seek advice from an AI.
- I would ride in an autonomously driving car.
- I would let an AI treat me instead of a human doctor in a GP practice.
- There are many beneficial applications of AI.
- AI can have positive impacts on people’s wellbeing.
- I believe that AI will improve my life.
- AI has more disadvantages than advantages. R
- AI will cause many job losses. R


#### Trust Measure from Optimized - Propensity to Trust Questionnaire

10. I am likely to trust an automated system even when I have little knowledge about it
13. I rather trust an automated system than mistrust it

2. The developers of the STAR system are trustworthy
